default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1348.title: Negative-autocorrelation regime bounce
E-1348.hypothesis: When recent bar-to-bar changes alternate in sign (negative lag-1 autocorrelation), liquidity providers are being paid for bouncing; a bar larger than the recent std is likely to partly reverse.

E-1349.title: Key reversal bar at a lookback extreme
E-1349.hypothesis: A bar that sweeps the N-bar low (high) and closes above the previous bar's high (below its low) shows stops were run and absorbed; follow the reversal.

E-1350.title: RSI(14) recross in a choppy tape
E-1350.hypothesis: In a low-efficiency (choppy) tape an RSI exit from an extreme marks the end of an overshoot; trade the return toward the middle.

E-1351.title: Regression-slope t-stat trend start
E-1351.hypothesis: A statistically significant slope of the intraday path (t-stat crossing a threshold) separates a persistent one-sided flow from noise; follow it as institutional execution continues.

E-1352.title: Volume climax without follow-through
E-1352.hypothesis: A high-volume directional bar followed by a bar that closes back against it marks exhausted aggressors; fade the climax.

E-1353.title: Walking the rolling band
E-1353.hypothesis: Staying in the top (bottom) fifth of the rolling range for several consecutive bars shows persistent one-sided demand; follow the start of the walk.

E-1354.title: Smoothed-price turn after a run
E-1354.hypothesis: After the EMA has fallen (risen) for several bars, its first upward (downward) tick shows selling pressure has stopped; trade the turn.

E-1355.title: Heikin-Ashi colour flip after a run
E-1355.hypothesis: A Heikin-Ashi candle that changes colour after a run of the opposite colour filters noise and marks a change of the dominant side.

E-1356.title: Body-efficiency exhaustion fade
E-1356.hypothesis: When nearly all of the recent range is captured by same-direction candle bodies, the move is one-sided and stretched; fade the first time the efficiency crosses the threshold.

E-1357.title: Bar-open gap rejection
E-1357.hypothesis: A bar that opens beyond the previous bar's extreme by a multiple of the typical range and closes back inside its own open direction shows the gap was an overreaction by market orders; fade it.
